task_row_model.query: I'm getting TypeError: sequence item 0: expected str instance, int found when using ','.join(my_list) in Python. How can I fix this error and what are the recommended ways to produce a comma-separated string from a list of integers?

documents.content: The str.join method expects the elements of the iterable to be the same string type as the separator. A common error occurs when trying to join bytes and str: for example b','.join([b'a', 'b']) will raise a TypeError. The solution is to ensure all elements are bytes or all are str, using element.encode() or element.decode() as appropriate, or use a bytes separator for byte sequences. This is often encountered in code handling binary data and text interchangeably.

documents.content: To produce comma-separated output from a list of integers without explicit conversion, you can use the print function with unpacking: print(*my_list, sep=','). This prints the elements separated by commas to standard output without creating a single string object. For building a single string, list comprehensions like [str(x) for x in nums] create string representations that you can then manipulate. These approaches are useful for quick output or display but don't address why ','.join on a list of ints raises a TypeError directly.

documents.content: The join method requires an iterable of strings; calling ','.join(my_list) raises TypeError if elements are not str. To fix it, convert elements to strings: ','.join(map(str, my_list)) or ','.join(str(x) for x in my_list). You can also build a list first: ','.join([str(x) for x in my_list]). For printing without creating a string, use print(*my_list, sep=','). Best practice is to explicitly convert non-string items to strings so the intention is clear; map(str, ...) and generator expressions avoid creating an intermediate list.

For printing without creating a string, use print(*my_list, sep=',').
